audit.whatIsWrong: Both layers read Jax/Skill/Sion/Sion/Jax/Sion/Sion. The packet and the mirror audit (jax__sion) both give Sion/Skill/Jax/Jax/Skill/Jax/Sion, and the page's own whys argue that version row for row.
audit.why: whys[2] says level 3 tips 'firmly in his favor', whys[3] calls charging into him at 4-5 suicidal, whys[4] calls level 6 a skill read, whys[5] calls first item 'his hardest power window'. Four rows rendered the opposite of their own paragraph.
audit.corrected: Chart set to Sion/Skill/Jax/Jax/Skill/Jax/Sion in both layers as one group, ratings following the file's Sion-perspective convention.

audit.whatIsWrong: phases[2].why, phases[3].why and phases[5].why all claim Sion-owned windows on rows that belong to Jax — phases[5] says 'Heartsteel is your spike' where the content layer says Trinity Force is his hardest power window.
audit.why: Sheen arrives before Heartsteel compounds; your spike is the two-item row, which the chart already gives you.
audit.corrected: Three phase whys rewritten to their own sides, with Counter Strike's 17s carried into phases[3].

audit.whatIsWrong: Two things. Counter Strike's cooldown is never given anywhere (it is 17/15/13/11/9 — the longest window in the matchup), and the page treats it as blanking your whole kit: wants.foe[0] says he 'activates Counter Strike to dodge your charged Q'. Riot's text says it dodges incoming ATTACKS. Separately, mid names his ultimate 'Grandmaster's Might'; the ability is Grandmaster-at-Arms.
audit.why: Counter Strike dodging basic attacks but not abilities is the difference between standing there doing nothing and continuing to land Decimating Smash and Roar of the Slayer through it — for a champion whose damage is almost entirely abilities, this is the most useful fact in the lane, and the page currently teaches the opposite. The wrong ultimate name is the same class of error as the calibration list.
audit.corrected: 17s stated in whys[3], phases[3] and wants.foe[0]; the attacks-not-abilities line written into wants.you[0] and whys[3]; Grandmaster-at-Arms corrected in mid with its 110s added; Empower's wind-up tell added to spikes[2].

edits.after: His lane - Counter Strike is 17s at rank 1 and covers every step-up. Farm safe and commit only in the gap after he spends it.

edits.after: Trinity Force beats Heartsteel to the punch - his Sheen burst arrives before your HP does.

edits.before: Counter Strike makes charging your Q into him suicidal at levels 4-5; he dodges the auto follow-up, stuns you, and your W-shield expires before it can be detonated usefully.
edits.after: Counter Strike is 17s at rank 1 and dodges attacks, not abilities — your Q and E still land through it, but the stun eats your auto follow-up and your shield times out.

edits.before: Jax with Trinity Force or Sheen is your hardest window — his Q-auto-E combo spikes sharply and your HP shield cannot absorb the burst before his stun locks you out of detonating it.
edits.after: Trinity Force Jax is your hardest window — the Empower wind-up (3-7s cooldown) is the tell his burst is coming, and the stun locks you out before the shield detonates.

edits.before: Levels 4 and 5 are Jax's lane. He can activate Counter Strike pre-emptively when he sees your Q charge animation and you have no reliable way to force damage through it. Farm safely, keep your W-shield for reactive use when he dashes in, and shove him under tower if the wave permits — his Counter Strike does not stop a tower shot. At level 6 the matchup opens up: Unstoppable Onslaught covers too much distance for Counter Strike to buy him a clean escape, and landing the follow-up E armor-shred then W-shield into a charged Q is a real kill threat. However his R grants substantial armor and MR on activation, so wait for it to drop before committing the all-in if he is already low — fighting into active Grandmaster's Might halves the damage your combo does.
edits.after: Levels 4 and 5 are Jax's lane. He can activate Counter Strike pre-emptively when he sees your Q charge animation, though it dodges attacks rather than abilities. Farm safely, keep your W-shield for reactive use when he dashes in, and shove him under tower if the wave permits — his Counter Strike does not stop a tower shot. At level 6 the matchup opens up: Unstoppable Onslaught covers too much distance for Counter Strike to buy him a clean escape, and landing the follow-up E armor-shred then W-shield into a charged Q is a real kill threat. However his R grants armor and MR on activation, so wait for it to drop before committing the all-in if he is already low — fighting into active Grandmaster-at-Arms halves the damage your combo does.

edits.before: Land a fully charged Q knockup through an E armor-shred into a W-shield detonation to punish him before Counter Strike stun lands
edits.after: Keep landing Q and E while Counter Strike is active — it blanks basic attacks, not abilities, so only your autos are wasted

edits.before: Activate Counter Strike to dodge your charged Q, then stun you out of W detonation so the shield expires unused
edits.after: Bait your autos into Counter Strike (17s at rank 1) — it dodges basic attacks, so your basics do nothing while it is up

notes: The wants.foe[0] claim that Counter Strike 'dodges your charged Q' is a real gameplay error, not just imprecision: Riot's text is 'dodge all incoming attacks', which is basic attacks. The page was telling a Sion player his ability damage is blanked when it is not. Left in place and unverified, matching the mirror's decision: early, mid, spikes[1] and the surrounding text assume Counter Strike's stun interrupts an in-progress Decimating Smash charge. Riot's text does not describe the charge as a channel and the kit carries no channel flag, so I rewrote wants.foe[0] around the verifiable attack-dodging instead of around the interrupt, and left the rest alone. Full-layer mojibake em dashes copied exactly in 'before', plain hyphens in 'after'.
